topic.name: Changing the Order of Integration in Triple Integrals: Changing Projection

question.text:
By changing the order of integration in the following repeated integrals so that they are integrated first with respect to $y,$ then $z,$ and then $x,$ express the following sum as a single repeated integral.

\[ \displaystyle \int_0^2 \int_0^{z/2} \int_{x}^{z+1} f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}z + \int_2^3 \int_0^{\sqrt{3-z}} \int_{x}^{z+1} f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}z \]
question.explanation:
We wish to find the limits of integration such that our integral can be expressed as \[ \int_a^b \int_{v_1(x)}^{v_2(x)} \int_{u_1(x,z)}^{u_2(x,z)} f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}x. \]

From the repeated integrals, we see that the domain of integration $R = R_1\cup R_2,$ where $R_1$ and $R_2$ are type III regions, is given by

\begin{align*} R_1 &= \left\{ (x,y,z) \: : \: 0 \leq z \leq 2, \:\: 0 \leq x \leq \dfrac{z}{2}, \:\: x\leq y \leq z+1 \right\}, \\[5pt] R_2 &= \left\{ (x,y,z) \: : \: 2 \leq z \leq 3, \:\: 0 \leq x \leq \sqrt{3-z}, \:\: x \leq y \leq z+1 \right\}. \end{align*}

Since all repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $y,$ the $y$-limits remain the same as before:

\[ \int_a^b \int_{v_1(x)}^{v_2(x)} \int_{x}^{z+1} f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}x \]

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $xz$-plane shown below.

The region $D$ consists of two type II regions in the $xz$-plane:

\[ D = \left\{ (x,z) \: : \: 0 \leq z \leq 2, \quad 0 \leq x \leq \dfrac{z}{2} \right\} \:\cup\: \left\{ (x,z) \: : \: 2 \leq z \leq 3, \quad 0 \leq x \leq \sqrt{3-z} \right\}. \]

To change the order of integration from $\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}z$ to $\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}x,$ we write $D$ as a type I region.

Notice that the bottom boundary of the region, written in the form $z=z(x),$ is \[ x=\dfrac{z}{2} \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad z = 2x \] and the top boundary of the region is \[ x=\sqrt{3-z} \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad z = -x^2+3. \]

Then, the type I representation of the region is

\[ D = \left\{ (x,z) \: : \: 0 \leq x \leq 1, \quad 2x \leq z \leq -x^2+3 \right\}, \]

as shown in the diagram below.

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

\[ \int_0^{\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{1}} \int_{\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{2x}}^{\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{-x^2+3}} \int_{x}^{z+1} f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}x. \]

example.title: Swapping the Order of Integration When the Projection Is Partitioned

question.text:
Evaluate $ \displaystyle \int_{0}^{\sqrt{\pi/2}} \int_{x}^{\sqrt{\pi/2}} \int_{0}^{y^2} \cos{z} \: \textrm{d}z \: \textrm{d}y \: \textrm{d}x. $

Hint: First change the order of integration to $\textrm{d}z \: \textrm{d}x \: \textrm{d}y.$
question.explanation:
We wish to find the limits of integration such that our integral can be expressed as \[ \int_{a}^{b} \int_{v_1(y)}^{v_2(y)} \int_{u_1(x,y)}^{u_2(x,y)} \cos{z} \:\textrm{d}z \: \textrm{d}x \: \textrm{d}y. \]

From the repeated integral, we see that the domain of integration $R$ can be written as a type I region as follows: \[ R = \left\{ (x,y,z) \: : \: 0 \leq x \leq \sqrt{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}, \:\: x \leq y \leq \sqrt{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}, \:\: 0 \leq z \leq y^2 \right\} \]

Since all repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $z,$ the $z$-limits remain the same as before: \[ \int_{a}^{b} \int_{v_1(y)}^{v_2(y)} \int_{0}^{y^2} \cos{z} \:\textrm{d}z \: \textrm{d}x \: \textrm{d}y \]

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $xy$-plane shown below.

The region $D$ is type I region in the $xy$-plane: \[ D = \left\{ (x,y) \::\: 0 \leq x \leq \sqrt{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}, \quad x \leq y \leq \sqrt{\dfrac{\pi}{2}} \right\}. \]

To change the order of integration from $\textrm{d}z \: \textrm{d}y \: \textrm{d}x$ to $\textrm{d}z \: \textrm{d}x \: \textrm{d}y,$ we write $D$ as a type II region.

Notice that the left boundary of the region $D$ is \[ x = 0 \] and the right boundary of the region, written in the form $x = x(y),$ is \[ y = x \qquad\Longrightarrow \qquad x = y. \]

Then, the type II representation of the region is \[ D = \left\{ (x,y) \::\: 0 \leq y \leq \sqrt{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}, \quad 0 \leq x \leq y \right\}, \]

as shown in the diagram below.

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain \begin{align*} \int_{0}^{\sqrt{\pi/2}} \int_{x}^{\sqrt{\pi/2}} \int_{0}^{y^2} \cos{z} \: \textrm{d}z \: \textrm{d}y \: \textrm{d}x & = \int_{0}^{\sqrt{\pi/2}} \int_{0}^{y} \int_{0}^{y^2} \cos{z} \: \textrm{d}z \: \textrm{d}x \: \textrm{d}y\\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{\sqrt{\pi/2}} \int_{0}^{y} \left[ \int_{0}^{y^2} \cos{z} \: \textrm{d}z \right] \textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}y\\[5pt] & = \int_{0}^{\sqrt{\pi/2}} \int_{0}^{y} \big[ \sin{z} \big]_{0}^{y^2} \: \textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}y \\[5pt] & = \int_{0}^{\sqrt{\pi/2}} \int_{0}^{y} \sin(y^2) \: \textrm{d}x \: \textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{\sqrt{\pi/2}} \sin(y^2) \left[ \int_{0}^{y} \textrm{d}x \right] \textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{\sqrt{\pi/2}} \sin(y^2) \big[ x \big]_{0}^{y} \:\textrm{d}y \\[5pt] %&= \int_{0}^{\sqrt{\pi/2}} \sin(y^2) \cdot y \:\textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{\sqrt{\pi/2}} y\sin(y^2) \:\textrm{d}y \\[5pt] & = \left[ -\dfrac{1}{2}\cos(y^2) \right]_{0}^{\sqrt{\pi/2}} \\[5pt] & =-\dfrac{1}{2} \left( \cos \dfrac{\pi}{2} - \cos 0 \right) \\[5pt] &= -\dfrac{1}{2}(0 - 1)\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{1}{2}. \end{align*}

example.title: Evaluating Triple Integrals by Changing the Projection Type

question.text:
Evaluate $ \displaystyle \int_{0}^{1} \int_{x^2}^{1} \int_{0}^{x} 4\sin(z^2) \: \textrm{d}y \: \textrm{d}z \: \textrm{d}x. $

Hint: First change the order of integration to $\textrm{d}y \: \textrm{d}x \: \textrm{d}z.$
question.explanation:
We wish to find the limits of integration such that our integral can be expressed as \[ \int_{a}^{b} \int_{v_1(z)}^{v_2(z)} \int_{u_1(x,z)}^{u_2(x,z)} 4\sin(z^2) \:\textrm{d}y \: \textrm{d}x \: \textrm{d}z. \]

From the repeated integral, we see that the domain of integration $R$ can be written as a type III region as follows: \[ R = \left\{ (x,y,z) \: : \: 0 \leq x \leq 1, \:\: x^2 \leq z \leq 1, \:\: 0 \leq y \leq x \right\} \]

Since all repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $y,$ the $y$-limits remain the same as before: \[ \int_{a}^{b} \int_{v_1(z)}^{v_2(z)} \int_{0}^{x} 4\sin(z^2) \:\textrm{d}y \: \textrm{d}x \: \textrm{d}z \]

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $xz$-plane shown below.

The region $D$ is type I region in the $xz$-plane: \[ D = \left\{ (x,z) \::\: 0 \leq x \leq 1, \quad x^2 \leq z \leq 1 \right\}. \]

To change the order of integration from $\textrm{d}y \: \textrm{d}z \: \textrm{d}x$ to $\textrm{d}y \: \textrm{d}x \: \textrm{d}z,$ we write $D$ as a type II region.

Notice that the left boundary of the region $D$ is \[ x = 0 \] and the right boundary of the region, written in the form $x = x(z),$ is \[ z = x^2 \qquad\Longrightarrow \qquad x = \sqrt{z}. \]

Then, the type II representation of the region is \[ D = \left\{ (x,z) \::\: 0 \leq z \leq 1, \quad 0 \leq x \leq \sqrt{z} \right\}, \]

as shown in the diagram below.

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain \begin{align*} \int_{0}^{1} \int_{x^2}^{1} \int_{0}^{x} 4\sin(z^2) \: \textrm{d}y \: \textrm{d}z \: \textrm{d}x & = \int_{0}^{1} \int_{0}^{\sqrt{z}} \int_{0}^{x} 4\sin(z^2) \: \textrm{d}y \: \textrm{d}x \: \textrm{d}z\\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{1} \int_{0}^{\sqrt{z}} \left[ \int_{0}^{x} 4\sin(z^2) \textrm{d}y \right] \textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}z\\[5pt] & = \int_{0}^{1} \int_{0}^{\sqrt{z}} 4\sin(z^2)\big[ y \big]_{0}^{x} \: \textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}z \\[5pt] & = \int_{0}^{1} \int_{0}^{\sqrt{z}} 4x\sin(z^2) \: \textrm{d}x \: \textrm{d}z \\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{1} 2\sin(z^2) \left[ \int_{0}^{\sqrt{z}} 2x \: \textrm{d}x \right] \textrm{d}z \\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{1} 2\sin(z^2) \big[ x^2 \big]_{0}^{\sqrt{z}} \:\textrm{d}z \\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{1} 2z\sin(z^2) \:\textrm{d}z \\[5pt] & = \left[ -\cos(z^2) \right]_{0}^{1} \\[5pt] &= -(\cos(1) - 1)\\[5pt] & = 1 - \cos(1). \end{align*}

example.title: Evaluating Triple Integrals by Changing the Projection Type

question.text:
By changing the order of integration, find the missing limits in the following repeated integral.

\[ \int_0^1 \int_{\sqrt{z}}^{e^{z}} \int_{z^2-1}^{x+z} \:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}z = \int_{0}^{1} \int_{0}^{\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{p}} \int_{z^2-1}^{x+z} \:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}x + \int_{1}^{\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{q}} \int_{\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{r}}^{1} \int_{z^2-1}^{x+z} \:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}x \]
question.explanation:
We wish to find the limits of integration such that our integral can be expressed as \[ \int_a^b \int_{v_1(x)}^{v_2(x)} \int_{u_1(x,z)}^{u_2(x,z)} \:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}x + \int_c^d \int_{v_3(x)}^{v_4(x)} \int_{u_3(x,z)}^{u_4(x,z)} \:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}x. \]

From the repeated integral, we see that the domain of integration $R$ can be written as a type III region as follows:

\[ R = \big\{ (x,y,z) \: : \: 0 \leq z \leq 1, \:\: \sqrt{z} \leq x \leq e^{z}, \:\: z^2-1 \leq y \leq x+z \big\} \]

Since all repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $y,$ the $y$-limits remain the same as before:

\[ \int_0^1 \int_{\sqrt{z}}^{e^{z}} \int_{z^2-1}^{x+z} \:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}z = \int_a^b \int_{v_1(x)}^{v_2(x)} \int_{z^2-1}^{x+z} \:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}x + \int_c^d \int_{v_3(x)}^{v_4(x)} \int_{z^2-1}^{x+z} \:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}x \]

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $xz$-plane shown below.

The region $D$ is a type II region in the $xz$-plane:

\[ D = \big\{ (x,z) \::\: 0 \leq z \leq 1, \quad \sqrt{z} \leq x \leq e^{z} \big\}. \]

To change the order of integration from $\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}z$ to $\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}x,$ we split $D$ into two type I regions.

Notice that the bottom and top boundaries of the left region, written in the form $z=z(x),$ are

$\qquad$ $z = 0\quad$ and $\quad z = x^2.$

Also, the bottom and top boundaries of the right region, written in the form $z=z(x),$ are

$\qquad$ $z = \ln{x} \quad$ and $\quad z =1.$

So, we can write $D$ as a union of

\[ D_1 = \big\{ (x,z) \::\: 0 \leq x \leq 1, \quad 0 \leq z \leq x^2 \big\} \]

and

\[ D_2 = \big\{ (x,z) \::\: 1 \leq x \leq e, \quad \ln{x} \leq z \leq 1 \big\}. \]

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

\begin{align*} \int_{0}^{1} \int_{0}^{\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{x^2}} \int_{z^2-1}^{x+z} \:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}x + \int_{1}^{\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{e}} \int_{\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\ln{x}}}^{1} \int_{z^2-1}^{x+z} \:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}x. \end{align*}

example.title: Swapping the Order of Integration When the Projection Is Partitioned

question.text:
By changing the order of integration, find the missing limits in the following repeated integral.

\[ \int_{-2}^0 \int_{(x^2-4)/2}^{(x+2)^3/4} \int_{x}^{y^2} \:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}x = \int_{\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{p}}^{0} \int_{\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{q}}^{0} \int_{x}^{y^2} \:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}y + \int_{0}^2 \int_{\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{r}}^{0} \int_{x}^{y^2} \:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}y \]
question.explanation:
We wish to find the limits of integration such that our integral can be expressed as \[ \int_a^b \int_{v_1(y)}^{v_2(y)} \int_{u_1(x,y)}^{u_2(x,y)} \:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}y + \int_c^d \int_{v_3(y)}^{v_4(y)} \int_{u_3(x,y)}^{u_4(x,y)} \:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}y. \]

From the repeated integral, we see that the domain of integration $R$ can be written as a type I region as follows:

\[ R = \left\{ (x,y,z) \: : \: -2 \leq x \leq 0, \:\: \dfrac{1}{2}(x^2-4) \leq y \leq \dfrac{1}{4}(x+2)^3, \:\: x \leq z \leq y^2 \right\} \]

Since all repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $z,$ the $z$-limits remain the same as before:

\[ \int_{-2}^0 \int_{(x^2-4)/2}^{(x+2)^3/4} \int_{x}^{y^2} \:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}x = \int_a^b \int_{v_1(y)}^{v_2(y)} \int_{x}^{y^2} \:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}y + \int_c^d \int_{v_3(y)}^{v_4(y)} \int_{x}^{y^2} \:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}y \]

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $xy$-plane shown below.

The region $D$ is a type I region in the $xz$-plane:

\[ D = \left\{ (x,y) \::\: -2 \leq x \leq 0, \quad \dfrac{1}{2}(x^2 - 4) \leq y \leq \dfrac{1}{4}(x+2)^3 \right\}. \]

To change the order of integration from $\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}x$ to $\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}y,$ we split $D$ into two type II regions.

Notice that the bottom and top boundaries of the lower region, written in the form $x=x(y),$ are

$\qquad$ $x = -\sqrt{2y+4} \quad$ and $\quad x =0.$

Also, the bottom and top boundaries of the upper region, written in the form $x=x(y),$ are

$\qquad$ $x = \sqrt[3]{4y}-2 \quad$ and $\quad x = 0.$

So, we can write $D$ as a union of

\[ D_1 = \big\{ (x,y) \::\: -2 \leq y \leq 0, \quad -\sqrt{2y+4} \leq x \leq 0 \big\} \]

and

\[ D_2 = \big\{ (x,y) \::\: 0 \leq y \leq 2, \quad \sqrt[3]{4y}-2 \leq x \leq 0 \big\}. \]

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

\begin{align*} \int_{\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{-2}}^{0} \int_{\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{-\sqrt{2y+4}}}^{0} \int_{x}^{y^2} \:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}y + \int_{0}^2 \int_{\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\sqrt[3]{4y}-2}}^{0} \int_{x}^{y^2} \:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}y. \end{align*}
